security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code, fenced Python examples, placeholder URLs, and Stripe object identifiers. The confirmed risk is insecure secret handling guidance because Stripe API key placeholders are hardcoded in examples. No evidence of prompt injection, malware intent, unauthorized network exfiltration, or system reconnaissance was found.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded Stripe API key placeholders in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Load API keys from environment variables or a secret manager, and document per-environment key separation.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded webhook signing secret in the webhook sample.
remediation.suggestion: Use a runtime setting such as STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and document rotation for webhook secrets.

remediation.issue: Placeholder redirect URLs are shown without deployment guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Explain that success, cancel, and return URLs must be configured as trusted URLs per environment.

content.value_statement: Stripe payment work needs secure checkout, billing, and webhook handling. This skill gives structured implementation patterns for payments, subscriptions, refunds, customers, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Explains hosted Checkout, Payment Intents, Setup Intents, and customer portal flows.
Provides Python examples for one-time payments, subscriptions, refunds, disputes, and customer records.
Shows webhook signature verification, event routing, and idempotent processing patterns.
Covers saved payment methods, default payment methods, and customer payment method listing.
Lists Stripe test cards and a basic test payment flow.
limitations: Examples are illustrative and require adaptation for each framework and deployment environment.
Referenced resource and asset files are not included in the scanned package.
The guide focuses on Python and Flask-style examples more than other stacks.
Production use still requires current Stripe documentation, SDK versions, and compliance review.

use_cases.title: Add SaaS Billing
use_cases.description: Plan subscription checkout, customer creation, saved payment methods, and billing portal access.

use_cases.title: Implement Payment Webhooks
use_cases.description: Design verified webhook handlers for successful payments, failed payments, and subscription cancellations.

use_cases.title: Handle Refund Operations
use_cases.description: Map refund, dispute, and payment method workflows into application service logic.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Checkout
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a hosted payment page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Stripe Checkout flow for my product. Include required inputs, success handling, cancellation handling, and test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Webhooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Stripe webhook endpoint for payment success, payment failure, and subscription cancellation. Include verification and idempotency.

prompt_templates.title: Build Subscriptions
prompt_templates.scenario: Recurring billing with saved payment methods.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a subscription billing flow with customers, prices, default payment methods, incomplete payments, and billing portal access.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Stripe payment integration for webhook safety, secret handling, retry behavior, testing coverage, and PCI scope.

output_examples.input: Plan a hosted checkout flow for a monthly subscription.
output: Recommended hosted Checkout for reduced PCI scope.
Required product, price, customer, success URL, and cancel URL decisions.
Webhook events needed for payment success, failure, and subscription cancellation.
Test plan using Stripe test mode before production keys.

output_examples.input: Review webhook handling for a Stripe integration.
output: Verify the Stripe signature before reading event data.
Store processed event identifiers to prevent duplicate fulfillment.
Return clear failure responses so Stripe retries temporary failures.
Route each supported event to a small application handler.
Create full or partial refunds against the payment intent.
Record refund reasons and customer-facing status changes.
Attach dispute evidence from verified order and communication records.

best_practices: Store Stripe API keys and webhook secrets in environment variables or a secret manager.
Verify webhook signatures and process Stripe events idempotently.
Use hosted Checkout or Stripe.js to reduce PCI scope and avoid raw card handling.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Stripe secret keys or webhook signing secrets in source files.
Do not trust client-side payment status without webhook confirmation.
Do not store or transmit raw card data through your application server.

faq.question: Can this skill build a complete Stripe integration?
faq.answer: It provides implementation patterns and examples. You still need to adapt them to your application and Stripe account.

faq.question: Does it support subscription billing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers products, prices, subscriptions, incomplete payments, saved payment methods, and the customer portal.

faq.question: Does it cover webhook security?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows signature verification, supported event routing, failure responses, and idempotent processing concepts.

faq.question: Is the guidance production ready?
faq.answer: It is a starting point. Production deployments need secret management, current SDK checks, monitoring, and compliance review.

faq.question: Which AI coding tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it replace Stripe documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use it with official Stripe documentation, especially for current API behavior and regional compliance requirements.
